findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mop to be resting on floor in dry storage area. Discussed with PIC, mop was moved to mop sink hanging area. Ensure mops are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed 2 coolers to have improper storage order of meats. Eggs and other meats were observed to be stored above salads. Discussed with PIC, meats were relocated to a proper location within cooler. Ensure facility is maintaining proper storage order of meats to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed salt, flour, and rice to be missing the proper labeling being contained outside of original container. Discussed with PIC, labels were placed on each container. Ensure any white substance removed from its original container is properly labeled.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed 2 containers of old, soiled utensils to be stored in contact with clean handing ladles. Discussed with PIC, the old utensils were no longer in use and discarded. The ladles were pulled to be placed in dish machine. Ensure clean utensils are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed both ice scoops to be resting on unsanitized surfaces. Discussed with PIC, ice scoops will be cleaned ad placed on a sanitized surface in between use. Ensure in use utensils are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair at the hand sink and to the left of dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring/replacing caulking regularly.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no working sani bucket upon entry to the kitchen. Employees were actively prepping food. Discussed creating a sani bucket prior to food engagement with PIC/employees. PIC made a sani bucket upon request - 400 ppm. Employees were in agreement to correct practice. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas no longer smooth and easily cleanable:
1. Kitchen hand sink needs re-caulked to the wall.
2. Dish machine area needs caulking: the caulk near the spray nozzle is molded and black (water exposure) and the area after the dish machine (drain board) has no caulk to the wall. Re-caulk/caulk the areas.

Discussed building repairs with PIC. Maintenance will correct the issues. Correct before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

On arrival, the PIC was able to only produce a blank copy of a reporting agreement. A discussion took place in relation to the requirements per the code. Multiple copies were made of the agreement and staff signed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the only sani bucket in the kitchen is observed to not produce a color change on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. The bucket was remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

There is a line of pink slime along the top of the ice machine where the water enters the area for freezing. PIC show the issue and the machine was cleaned during the inspection. The employees are aware that this area should be cleaned regularly to prevent accumulation of potentially pathogenic organisms.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Four large cans on the rack in the dry storage area are observed with large dents. One of those cans appears to be leaking as well. A discussion took place between the inspector and PIC explaining the relevant safety concerns of this situation. PIC is instructed to ensure that any cans with significant damage are moved to a separate area and returned to the supplier. The four cans in question were separated out during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. 

The blade of the can opener in the kitchen is observed soiled. Discussion with the PIC reveals that the can opener is cleaned every couple days. The can opener should be cleaned/ sanitized after becoming soiled. PIC ran the can opener through the dish machine during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) A container of marscopone cheese was observed with a date marking of 12/23. This exceeds the seven days allowed for TCS foods in a facility. The container was discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 307.11  (C) The deflector shield in the ice machine was observed with an accumulation of bacterial slime. PIC was instructed to clean and sanitize the location often enough so as to prevent the build up of possible pathogens and their contamination of ice underneath. The lip was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) The deflector shield in the ice machine was observed with an accumulation of bacterial slime. PIC was instructed to clean and sanitize the location often enough so as to prevent the build up of possible pathogens and their contamination of ice underneath.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11  (C) An opened and partially consumed bottle of Dr. Pepper was observed on the top door shelf in refrigerator #3. PIC was instructed to keep employee beverages separated from those intended for residents and stored in such a way as to not potentially contaminate those foods.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 (A) (2) (C) Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contaminations. 

A slime substance was observed forming on the deflector shield of the ice machine. Inspector discussed the cleaning practices and stated that the shield should be cleaned often enough so as to prevent accumulation. The shield was cleaned during the inspection.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

Observed the clean bowls and plates to be stored on a shelf with the food contact surfaces facing up. Discussed the possible potential issue of contamination with the PIC. A sheet of wax paper was placed over the items to protect them from future contamination during the inspection.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

1) the deflector shield in the ice machine is soiled
2) the can opener is soiled

PIC cleaned both occurrences and will ensure cleaning regularly to maintain clean.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.
Observed the sanitizer being used for wiping cloths to be reading well above acceptable ranges for CL (the strip bleached out on use). When notified, PIC reset each bucket by manually making the solution. GFS will be contacted for maintenance. A spot check will take place after maintenance.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed containers of white powder on the dry storage shelves to not be labeled with the common name of the contents. It appears as though these are sugar and flour and it was discussed that they need to be labeled as such. Label all items removed from their original container.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed raw chicken thawing in standing water in the third compartment of the three compartment sink. Water was drained from the sink and cold running water was turned on over the chicken. Proper thawing methods were discussed.
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No proof of Illinois FSSMC at the time of the inspection. The two employees who are present at the time of the inspection have proof of passing National Registry of Food Safety Professionals, however, they need to obtain the IL certificate. Once received, please email to inspector before the follow up date.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
1) Observed sloppy joes cooling with no time marked. The meat was marked with a time during the inspection. Properly cool the food. 2) Observed three containers of powder with what appears to be salt, sugar, and flour with no label. Provide a label on all unmistakable powders. The manager provided a label on all three containers to correct the violation during the inspection. 
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed a pie stored underneath raw meat in the reach in freezer. The pie was moved to a higher shelf during the inspection.
750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed the top interior of the microwave to have food splash. Clean the microwave. The manager washed the top interior of the microwave to correct the violation during the inspection.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed some spillage underneath the dry storage shelving. Clean the floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Observed no thermometer in a reach in cooler. A thermometer was replaced during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed some ice buildup in the dessert freezer. Clean the non-food contact surface.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak at the spray hose near the dish machine.  Repair the leak.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed a dog in the kitchen upon arrival of inspection.  The dog was removed immediately from the kitchen.
750-1400 Live animals including birds and turtles, shall be excluded from within the food service operational premises.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed bulk flour and salt not labeled.  Label the bulk containers with the proper common name.  (IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED)
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed the ice scoop in the ice machine laying in the ice.  Handle must be extended out of the food. (IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED)
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Sanitizing temperature
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine to be reaching 144 F.   For heat sanitizing, dish machine must reach 180 F. A heat sanitizing strip was placed on a plate and did not turn black.
750-830 All hot water for sanitizing dishes and equipment must be a minimum of 180F when it leaves the dishwashing machine manifold in order to kill pathogens.  Properly sanitize all items. Check and maintain the dishwasher frequently.
